assertions.name: normaliser_coefficients_are_the_binomial_coefficients
assertions.source: coefficients of q^{2k} in Z(n) = sum over partitions of s_lambda(1,q^2) * f^lambda, rebuilt from markov_weights_symbolic's own hook/Schur components, vs C(n,k) from the binomial theorem, n = 2..6. Agreement identifies Z(n) as the weight generating function of (C^2)^{tensor n} with q^{2k} counting k down-spins among n strands.

assertions.name: normaliser_at_q_one_is_the_hilbert_space_dimension
assertions.source: Z(n)|_{q=1} from the partition sum above vs 2^n = dim (C^2)^{tensor n} (independent: elementary linear algebra, not a corpus quantity), n = 2..6

assertions.name: every_registered_operator_class_vanishes_at_q_equals_one
assertions.source: max over the E_0 registry's operator classes of |value at q = 1|: convention A's Delta(net) = h(h-2)/2 with h = q - 1/q, and convention B's spectral block sum via b_over_a_evaluator.spectral_b_over_a(q=1.0) at D, 4He and 12C. All are identically zero: at q = 1 every one-crossing eigenvalue is +-1, so the Hecke algebra degenerates to C[S_n] and no deformation is left to carry an energy.

assertions.name: classical_entropy_is_the_majority_of_the_extensive_term
assertions.source: log 2 / log(1+q_0^2) = 0.86328133. The numerator is the q = 1 value, which survives where every operator class above is zero; the denominator is the full per-strand extensive term at q_0. A share above 1/2 means the extensive term is mostly the hbar_q^0 entropy.

assertions.name: landauer_temperature_hunt_found_no_candidate_scale
assertions.source: near_matches_5pct from computations/landauer-crossing-energy-probe.witness.json is empty for both proton and neutron; its implied kT_eff is ~17856 MeV/q-bit against five canonical candidate scales, with ratios running 41.8774x to 4271.6x. Different information measure from log Z, so suggestive rather than decisive here.

assertions.name: no_framework_scale_matches_the_temperature_log_Z_would_need
assertions.source: kT required for 3*log(1+q_0^2)*kT = a_V is 6.5593789 MeV; the nearest of the framework's canonical scales is m_e/hbar_q at ratio 1.27185, i.e. 27.19 % away. Asserting nothing is within 5 %. Back-computed from a_V, so this refutes an identification rather than establishing one.

description: Answers the qou-59j5 successor question with no energy scale: log Z carries hbar_q^0 and the framework assigns it no operator class. Z(n) is the weight generating function of (C^2)^{tensor n}, so log Z(3A) is a graded log-dimension -- an entropy. Every registered operator class vanishes at q=1; log Z does not, and 86.33% of it is the classical log 2. Comparing it to a_V is a category error.

temperature_hunt.why_a_temperature: F = -kT log Z. Entropy times temperature is an energy, so the objection 'log Z CAN become an energy' is correct. What the framework lacks is the kT, not the arithmetic.
temperature_hunt.why_E_0_is_not_it: every E_0 registry convention is (scale) x (hbar_q-suppressed operator), totalling hbar_q^2 (bean qou-59j5). Pairing that with an hbar_q^0 log-dimension breaks the registry's own index. E_0 is an action scale, not a temperature.

operator_classes_at_q_equals_one.why: at q = 1 the one-crossing eigenvalues (sym: q, 1/q, (q+1/q)/2; alt: their negatives; std: 1) all become +-1, so |Lambda_free/Lambda_nuc| = 1 and its log is 0. H_n(q) -> C[S_n].

hbar_q_grading_of_the_extensive_term.note: d/dq log(1+q^2) = 2q/(1+q^2) = 1 at q = 1 and the second derivative vanishes there, so the expansion is log 2 + (q-1) + O((q-1)^3). The residual measured above is consistent with that.

NOT_A_CANDIDATE.the_tempting_move: strip log 2 and call the remainder (q0 - 1) = 0.1099785828 per strand the deformation energy
NOT_A_CANDIDATE.why_it_is_not_reported_in_MeV: It would still be scale-ambiguous by the same 5.35x (convention A vs B, bean qou-59j5), so converting it would be picking a scale that lands somewhere -- the same fit this lane has walked into three times now. Recorded as a dimensionless measurement only.

data.what_this_explains: Why the EXPONENT test passed cleanly (qou-imcd: A-exponent exactly 1) while six magnitude ansaetze failed. An extensive entropy and an extensive energy have the same A-scaling by construction, so the exponent test cannot distinguish them. The magnitude ansaetze were fitting a conversion between two different KINDS of quantity, which is why they failed 'all in the same way'.
data.verdict: log Z carries hbar_q^0 and has no operator class. Z(n) = sum_k C(n,k) q^{2k} is the weight generating function of (C^2)^{tensor n} and Z(n)|_{q=1} = 2^n is its dimension, so log Z(3A) is a graded log-dimension -- an ENTROPY. Every operator class the E_0 registry indexes vanishes at q = 1; log Z does not, and 86.33% of it is that classical log 2. Comparing log Z(3A)*E_0 to a_V is a CATEGORY ERROR, independently of which E_0 is chosen. Every deficit reported this session -- 1.57x, 6.9x, 8.38x, 12.84x -- was an entropy measured against an energy through an undetermined conversion. The successor question is closed and the answer removes the comparison rather than settling it.
